arxiv-2102-13189.title: Rip van Winkle’s Razor: A Simple Estimate of Overfit to Test Data
arxiv-2102-13189.creator: Sanjeev Arora, Yi Zhang
arxiv-2102-13189.description: Abstract Traditional statistics forbids use of test data (a.k.a. holdout data) during training. Dwork et al. 2015 pointed out that current practices in machine learning, whereby researchers build upon each other’s models, copying hyperparameters and even computer code—amounts to implicitly training on the test set. Thus error rate on test data may not reflect the true population error.

arxiv-2201-07629.title: Comment on “Explicit Analytical Solution for Random Close Packing in d = 2 d=2 and d = 3 d=3 ”
arxiv-2201-07629.creator: Patrick Charbonneau, Peter K. Morse
arxiv-2201-07629.description: Abstract A recent letter proposes a first-principle computation of the random close packing (RCP) density in spatial dimensions d=2 and d=3 Zaccone 2022 . This problem has a long history of such proposals Williams 1998 ; Jalali and Li 2004 ; Kamien and Liu 2007 ; Song et al. 2008 ; Jin et al.

arxiv-2204-06911.title: Robust Bayesian inference in complex models with possibility theory
arxiv-2204-06911.creator: Jeremie Houssineau
arxiv-2204-06911.description: Abstract We propose a general solution to the problem of robust Bayesian inference in complex settings where outliers may be present. In practice, the automation of robust Bayesian analyses is important in the many applications involving large and complex datasets.

arxiv-2206-06320.title: Cryptocurrency Bubble Detection: A New Stock Market Dataset, Financial Task & Hyperbolic Models
arxiv-2206-06320.creator: Ramit Sawhney, Shivam Agarwal, Vivek Mittal, Paolo Rosso, Vikram Nanda, Sudheer Chava
arxiv-2206-06320.description: Abstract The rapid spread of information over social media influences quantitative trading and investments. The growing popularity of speculative trading of highly volatile assets such as cryptocurrencies and meme stocks presents a fresh challenge in the financial realm. Investigating such "bubbles" - periods of sudden anomalous behavior of markets are critical in better understanding investor behavior and market dynamics.

arxiv-2207-11062.title: Lie groups and Chern-Simons Theory
arxiv-2207-11062.creator: Benjamin Himpel
arxiv-2207-11062.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Benjamin Himpel. Witten introduced classical Chern-Simons theory to topology in 1989, when he defined an invariant for knots in 3-manifolds by an integral over a certain infinite-dimensional space, which up to today have not been entirely understood. However, they motivated lots of interesting questions and results in knot theory and low-dimensional topology, as well as the development of entirely new fields. These are lecture notes for a course in Lie groups and Chern-Simons Theory aimed at graduate students.

arxiv-2212-10373.title: Bateman–Horn, polynomial Chowla and the Hasse principle with probability 1
arxiv-2212-10373.creator: Tim Browning, Efthymios Sofos, Joni Teräväinen
arxiv-2212-10373.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Tim Browning, Efthymios Sofos, Joni Teräväinen. With probability 1 1 , we assess the average behaviour of various arithmetic functions at the values of degree d d polynomials f ∈ ℤ ⁡ [ t ] f\in\mathbb{Z}[t] that are ordered by height. This allows us to establish averaged versions of the Bateman–Horn conjecture, the polynomial Chowla conjecture and to address a basic question about the integral Hasse principle for norm form equations.

arxiv-2305-01064.title: Questions and Concerns About Google’s Quantum Supremacy Claim
arxiv-2305-01064.creator: Gil Kalai, Yosef Rinott, Tomer Shoham
arxiv-2305-01064.description: Abstract In October 2019, Nature published a paper [ 6 ] describing an experimental work that was performed at Google. The paper claims to demonstrate quantum (computational) supremacy on a 53-qubit quantum computer. Since then we have been involved in a long-term project to study various statistical aspects of the Google experiment.

arxiv-2311-18450.title: Lessons from Building StackSpot AI : A Contextualized AI Coding Assistant Conference: 46th International Conference on Software Engineering; April 2024; Lisbon, Portugal 46th International Conference on Software Engineering Price: 15.00 DOI: 10.1145/3613372.3614197 ISBN: 979-8-4007-0787-2/23/09 Pric
arxiv-2311-18450.creator: Gustavo Pinto, Cleidson de Souza, João Batista Neto, Alberto de Souza, Tarcísio Gotto, Edward Monteiro
arxiv-2311-18450.description: Abstract . With their exceptional natural language processing capabilities, tools based on Large Language Models (LLMs) like ChatGPT and Co-Pilot have swiftly become indispensable resources in the software developer’s toolkit. While recent studies suggest the potential productivity gains these tools can unlock, users still encounter drawbacks, such as generic or incorrect answers.

arxiv-2312-04801.title: Large- N N Principal Chiral Model in Arbitrary External Fields
arxiv-2312-04801.creator: Vladimir Kazakov, Evgeny Sobko, Konstantin Zarembo
arxiv-2312-04801.description: Abstract We report the explicit solution for the vacuum state of the two-dimensional S ​ U ​ ( N ) SU(N) Principal Chiral Model at large- N N for an arbitrary set of chemical potentials and any interaction strength, a unique result of such kind for an asymptotically free QFT.

arxiv-2411-08751.title: Generalized coupled cluster theory for ground and excited state intersections
arxiv-2411-08751.creator: Federico Rossi, Eirik F. Kjønstad, Sara Angelico, Henrik Koch
arxiv-2411-08751.description: Abstract Coupled cluster theory in the standard formulation is unable to correctly describe conical intersections among states of the same symmetry. This limitation has restricted the practical application of an otherwise highly accurate electronic structure model, particularly in nonadiabatic dynamics. Recently, the intersection problem among the excited states was fully characterized and resolved.

arxiv-2502-10377.title: Scene-Level Appearance Transfer with Semantic Correspondences 66 Conference: Special Interest Group on Computer Graphics and Interactive Techniques Conference Conference Papers ; August 10–14, 2025; Vancouver, BC, Canada Special Interest Group on Computer Graphics and Interactive Techniques Conferen
arxiv-2502-10377.creator: Liyuan Zhu, Shengqu Cai, Shengyu Huang, Gordon Wetzstein, Naji Khosravan, Iro Armeni
arxiv-2502-10377.description: Abstract . We introduce ReStyle3D, a novel framework for scene-level appearance transfer from a single style image to a real-world scene represented by multiple views. The method combines explicit semantic correspondences with multi-view consistency to achieve precise and coherent stylization.

arxiv-2503-18893.title: xKV: Cross-Layer KV-Cache Compression via Aligned Singular Vector Extraction
arxiv-2503-18893.creator: Chi-Chih Chang, Wei-Cheng Lin, Chien-Yu Lin, Hung-Yueh Chiang, Yash Akhauri, Yucheng Li, Huiqiang Jiang, Xilai Dai, Luis Ceze, Kai-Chiang Wu, Mohamed Abdelfattah
arxiv-2503-18893.description: Abstract Long-context Large Language Models (LLMs) enable powerful applications but incur high memory costs due to the key-value states (KV-Cache). Recent studies attempt to share KV-Cache across layers, but these approaches either require expensive pretraining or rely on per-token cross-layer cosine similarity that is often limited in practice.

arxiv-2512-03824.title: The impact of our peculiar motion on primordial non-Gaussianity measurements using the LIGER4GAL framework
arxiv-2512-03824.creator: Bartolomeo Bottazzi Baldi, Mohamed Yousry Elkhashab, Daniele Bertacca, Cristiano Porciani
arxiv-2512-03824.description: Abstract Current and forthcoming galaxy surveys will map the observable Universe with unprecedented depth, sky coverage, and precision. These maps are affected by relativistic redshift-space distortions (RSDs), which become increasingly relevant on ultra-large scales. Accurate modelling of these relativistic RSDs is essential to avoid systematic biases in key cosmological measurements, such as primordial non-Gaussianity (PNG).

arxiv-2602-04689.title: Static and auto-regressive neural emulation of phytoplankton biomass dynamics from physical predictors in the global ocean
arxiv-2602-04689.creator: Mahima Lakra 1 2, Ronan Fablet 2 4, Lucas Drumetz 2 4, Etienne Pauthenet 3, Elodie Martinez 3
arxiv-2602-04689.description: Abstract Phytoplankton is the basis of marine food webs, driving both ecological processes and global biogeochemical cycles. Despite their ecological and climatic significance, accurately simulating phytoplankton dynamics remains a major challenge for biogeochemical numerical models due to limited parameterizations, sparse observational data, and the complexity of oceanic processes.

pmc-10748420.title: Memantine protects the cultured rat hippocampal neurons treated by NMDA and amyloid β1–42
pmc-10748420.creator: Nataliia M. Rozumna, Vita V. Hanzha, Elena A. Lukyanetz
pmc-10748420.description: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a devastating neurodegenerative condition with no effective treatments. Recent research highlights the role of NMDA receptors in AD development, as excessive activation of these receptors triggers excitotoxicity. Memantine, an NMDA receptor antagonist, shows promise in curbing excitotoxicity.

pmc-11424800.title: Dual treatment approach for leiomyomas of urinary bladder: Experience from tertiary hospital
pmc-11424800.creator: Geofrey Chiloleti, Isaack Mlatie, Salim Sobbo, Mariam A. Mbezi, Herry G. Kibona, Fransia A. Mushi
pmc-11424800.description: Introduction and importanceLeiomyomas are rare, benign mesenchymal tumors. They represent 1 to 5 % of all urinary bladder tumors. 20 % are asymptomatic, but most presentations are voiding and storage, followed by hematuria. Surgery has been reported to be a standard treatment, depending on the size of the tumor and its location in the bladder.

pmc-11435033.title: Molecular Epidemiology of Hepatitis D Virus in the North-East Region of Romania
pmc-11435033.creator: Laura Iulia Grecu, Mariana Pavel-Tanasa, Lilia Matei, Camelia Sultana, Simona Maria Ruta, Razvan Ioan Grecu, Ramona Gabriela Ursu, Petru Cianga, Luminita Smaranda Iancu
pmc-11435033.description: The hepatitis D virus (HDV) superinfection of individuals with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection causes severe liver damage and the poorest long-term prognosis among viral hepatitis. This is attributed to the unique pathogenic mechanisms of HDV characterized by a direct cytopathic effect on hepatocytes and a significant impairment of the host immune response.

pmc-12837285.title: Methylglyoxal potentiates palmitic acid-induced endothelial dysfunction and atherogenesis in human endothelial cells
pmc-12837285.creator: Banafsheh Yalameha, Alireza Nourazarian, Reza Rahbarghazi, Delara Laghousi, Fatemeh Khaki-Khatibi
pmc-12837285.description: BackgroundEndothelial dysfunction is a key pathological mechanism in atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, and methylglyoxal (MGO) has been identified as a major contributor to endothelial cell damage through its overabundance. In this study, the effects of MGO on atherosclerotic human endothelial cells were investigated.

pmc-13589589.title: Diagnostic Performance of Diffusion-Weighted MRI and ADC Values in Differentiating Atypical Leiomyomas from Uterine Sarcomas
pmc-13589589.creator: Ramona-Andreea Rizescu, Iulia Alecsandra Salcianu, Alexandre Ionescu, Gheorghe Iana, Ana Magdalena Bratu, Ioana-Andreea Gheonea
pmc-13589589.description: Background: Leiomyomas are the most common benign uterine tumors, whereas uterine sarcomas are rare malignant neoplasms associated with high morbidity and mortality. Differentiation using imaging remains challenging because of overlapping radiologic features. Purpose: To evaluate magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) characteristics of atypical leiomyomas and uterine sarcomas, with emphasis on diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) values.

pmc-13610641.title: Research Progress and Prospects of Molecular Marker Technology on Jujube Trees
pmc-13610641.creator: Yanxu Liu, Ruijia Li, Zhihui Zhao, Mengjun Liu, Lili Wang
pmc-13610641.description: Jujube is an important fruit tree and one of the five major economic forest tree species native to China, possessing high nutritional and medicinal value. It plays a key supporting role in the efficient utilization of marginal land resources—such as mountainous, sandy, saline-alkali, and drought-prone areas—as well as in the revitalization of rural industries.
